concept: Index build commit quorum and hung builds
summary: Source-anchored research for Index build commit quorum and hung builds. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: For simultaneous replicated builds, votingMembers is the default commit quorum and requires all data-bearing voting members, including the primary, to become ready before commit. (high confidence)

SERVER-71768 reports Atlas builds stalling when a secondary already has the index and skips voting, with interrupted rolling builds suspected. Its documented workaround is adjusting the quorum. (medium confidence)
setIndexCommitQuorum has no effect on a build started with commitQuorum: 0. Members configured with buildIndexes: false cannot participate in a commit quorum. (low confidence)

SERVER-56976 records a historical bug where changing quorum failed to wake a build already waiting for votes. The issue lists fixes in 4.4.7, 5.0.0-rc0, and 5.1.0-rc0; this does not establish failure in current versions. (low confidence)
setIndexCommitQuorum cannot alter a build started with commitQuorum: 0. (low confidence)
A member configured with buildIndexes: false cannot participate in commit quorum; a voting member with this setting prevents use of votingMembers. (high confidence)

Starting in MongoDB 7.1, low disk space can trigger index-build abortion, but a member that has already voted to commit cannot retract its vote to request abortion. Do not assume the disk-space threshold always stops a waiting build. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Percona reproduced a default-quorum build waiting with one of three data-bearing members down; currentOp showed "Index Build: draining writes received during build". This message can therefore reflect quorum waiting rather than ongoing application writes. (medium confidence)
The default commitQuorum is "votingMembers": all data-bearing voting replica-set members. An unreachable required member can leave an index build hanging until it returns. (medium confidence)

Members vote after scanning the collection and the first side-write drain. While awaiting the commit decision, the build continues applying side writes; finishing the scan is not equivalent to completing the build. (high confidence)
setIndexCommitQuorum changes an in-progress build’s quorum. indexNames must include the entire group of indexes created by its single createIndexes operation. (high confidence)
Lowering commit quorum can let the primary commit sooner, but an unfinished secondary receiving commitIndexBuild can block further oplog application until its local build finishes. (high confidence)

Commit quorum controls readiness before primary commit. Starting in MongoDB 8.0, write concern waits for replication of the index-build oplog entry; earlier releases waited for the specified nodes to finish building the index. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

SERVER-87929 reports that changing a member's votes to zero did not update the quorum of an already-running build until primary stepdown or explicit quorum adjustment. The issue was resolved Won't Do in April 2024; treat this as a documented case, not a universal current-version guarantee. (low confidence)

In a 2020 firsthand report, a four-document collection hung with the draining-writes message despite no application writes. The author reported a node self-communication problem and a keyfile-related resolution after consulting MongoDB; this is historical case evidence, not a universal workaround. (low confidence)

SERVER-115085 describes an initial-sync member delaying index-build quorum until collection cloning finishes and index-build oplog entries are applied. The proposed automatic adjustment was closed Works as Designed, so the proposal is not evidence that automatic quorum reduction shipped. (low confidence)
The manual directs operators to dropIndexes or its shell helpers to stop in-progress replicated builds, and warns against using killOp for replica sets or sharded clusters. (low confidence)
An unreachable data-bearing voter can hold a default-quorum index build indefinitely; Percona reproduced a build completing after the missing third member returned. (high confidence)

Inference: quorum waiting can prolong the lifetime of active builds, so increasing maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds does not repair an unsatisfied quorum and can admit additional resource-consuming work. (medium confidence)
